hints: Form both vectors from $B$ or both towards $B$; direction does not affect length.
Equate squared lengths and cancel the $p^2$ terms.
Set $p=1$ and use vectors $\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ at vertex $B$.
Compute their dot product and moduli; then use the inverse cosine.
walkthrough: $\overrightarrow{AB}=(-1,2,5)$ and $\overrightarrow{CB}=(-4,5,-1)$; reversing both gives the angle at $B$. Their dot product is $4+10-5=9$.
$|AB|=\sqrt{30}$ and $|CB|=\sqrt{42}$, so $\cos\angle ABC=\frac9{\sqrt{30}\sqrt{42}}$. Thus $\angle ABC=75.3^\circ$ (3 s.f.).
